items.md: ## **ABSTRACT**
items.value: ABSTRACT

items.md: This article discusses the thermal noise source of electrocardiogram (ECG) applications based on the <u>ADS1298</u> and <u>ADS1298R</u> family of multichannel, simultaneous sampling, 24-bit, delta-sigma (ΔΣ) analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This report offers several observations on identifying the major sources of thermal noise in an ECG system, and recommends a method to improve thermal noise performance.
items.value: This article discusses the thermal noise source of electrocardiogram (ECG) applications based on the <u>ADS1298</u> and <u>ADS1298R</u> family of multichannel, simultaneous sampling, 24-bit, delta-sigma (ΔΣ) analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This report offers several observations on identifying the major sources of thermal noise in an ECG system, and recommends a method to improve thermal noise performance.

items.md: ## **1 Introduction**
items.value: 1 Introduction

items.md: The Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI) specifications allow 30-μV<sub>PP</sub> noise at 150-Hz bandwidth during a 10-second recording. The primary sources of thermal noise in an ECG system are generally caused by either resistors or amplifiers. This stochastic noise is specified as *root-mean-square (RMS) noise*, and is proportional to the square root of the noise bandwidth.
items.value: The Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI) specifications allow 30-μV<sub>PP</sub> noise at 150-Hz bandwidth during a 10-second recording. The primary sources of thermal noise in an ECG system are generally caused by either resistors or amplifiers. This stochastic noise is specified as root-mean-square (RMS) noise, and is proportional to the square root of the noise bandwidth.

items.md: Considering that the bulk of the system noise is Gaussian in nature, computed as RMS but specified by AAMI as peak-to-peak, we must develop a scale factor that gives us a confidence level that the peak-to-peak noise will not exceed 30 μV in any 10-second recording (5000 samples at 500 Hz). That level of confidence (1 part in 5000) equates to approximately 8σ. RMS is, by definition, 1σ, so we must have an RMS noise level approximately 1/8 the AAMI peak-to-peak specification, or 3.75-μV<sub>RMS</sub>.

2.3  ADS1298/98R Noise

items.md: Based on the information provided in the <u>ADS1298/98R product data sheet,</u> the noise measurement is taken with an internal reference, which includes the internal reference output noise. If we use a low-noise external reference, such as the <u>REF5025,</u> we can achieve better noise performance with a low gain setting. (The 2.5-V reference of the REF5025 output noise is 7.5 μV<sub>PP</sub> at 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz; higher frequency noise is filtered by the reference output capacitor.) A minimum of 1000 consecutive readings are then used to calculate the RMS and peak-to-peak noise for each reading.
